entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Abu Madyan Shu\u02c9yib ibn al-Husayn al-Ansari al-Andalusi, commonly known as Ab\u016f Madyan, was an influential Andalusian mystic and a great Sufi master. He was born in the late 12th century in Granada, Al-Andalus (present-day Spain), during the reign of the Almohad Caliphate. Abu Madyan spent his life traveling through the Iberian Peninsula, sharing his spiritual teachings and attracting a large following. His teachings emphasized the importance of love, compassion, and self-purification, and he was particularly known for his use of the mystical poem, the 'Dhikr', to guide his followers. Abu Madyan's legacy extended beyond his own lifetime, as his teachings influenced the development of Sufism in the Middle East and North Africa. He died in 1198, and his tomb in Granada remains a place of pilgrimage for Sufi Muslims to this day.
